subject: Clarifying SOC 2 applicability across hosting modes for Orchard Bank procurement
messages:
From: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@orchardbank.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@orchardbank.com>
Date: 2027-07-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SOC 2 evidence and scope question for hosting modes

Hi Mateo,

We're putting together our vendor SOC/compliance packet for the upcoming procurement review. A couple of clarifying questions from our security team:

1) Can you confirm whether Redwood's SOC 2 Type II report and the associated evidence cover work performed in Dedicated (reserved) GPU pools and in customer-managed VPC/Private deployments, or is coverage limited to the hosted API only?
2) For Dedicated pools: if a customer is placed in a dedicated pool but traffic can occasionally overflow to shared capacity (burst), how is that handled with respect to the audit boundary?
3) If a Private/VPC deployment is desired, what is the recommended path for Orchard Bank to get a formal attestation (bridge letter, separate report, or customer-specific scope confirmation)?

I've attached our SIG questionnaire and a short list of items the procurement team would like to see. Could you point us to the right artifacts and any bridge-letter templates if applicable?

Thanks — we'd like to review this before the vendor risk meeting next Wednesday.

Best,
Alex Ramos
Director, Cloud Security
Orchard Bank
[Attachment: Audit_Questionnaire_SIG.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@orchardbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-18T13:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 evidence and scope question for hosting modes

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear questions and for sharing the SIG. High-level answers up front, then a short suggested next step:

- SOC 2 Type II report (most recent period attached) covers our hosted API and ingress/egress, control plane, and the multitenant serving runtime as exercised during the audit period.
- Dedicated (reserved) GPU pools are included in our Type II report when they are part of Redwood-managed infrastructure under the audited control environment. In practice, Dedicated pools that are provisioned and operated by Redwood (even though reserved for a customer) are within the audit boundary.
- Private/VPC/on-prem deployments where the customer controls the compute/network (customer-managed runtime) are not typically part of Redwood's hosted Type II report. For those we provide a bridge letter or a tailored attestation describing which control activities we retain vs. those the customer is responsible for.

Burst behavior: if a Dedicated pool is configured with automatic burst-to-shared fallback, requests that route to shared capacity are within the audited environment only if the shared path is within the audited period and control set; otherwise they create an exception that we surface in a bridge letter.

Next step: can you confirm which of the following Orchard uses?
• Hosted API (all requests go to Redwood-hosted multitenant runtime)
• Dedicated (Redwood-managed, reserved pool) — do you have a tenant-id / project mapping?
• Private/VPC (customer-managed runtime in your environment)

I'll attach our SOC 2 PDF and a bridge-letter template draft. If you like, we can hop on a 30-minute call to walk the procurement and security teams through the mapping.

Regards,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Trust & Security
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026-07-01_to_2027-06-30.pdf]
[Attachment: bridge_letter_template.docx]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-18T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Orchard Bank scope follow-up (tenant mapping & evidence list)

Internal notes before the call:

Alex asked specifically about Dedicated pools and burst-to-shared behavior. Action items to prepare:
- Pull the tenant->pool mapping CSV for Orchard (example attached). Confirm whether their instances have 'burst' enabled.
- Mark which controls in the Type II map to dedicated-pool operations (patching, access control, logging, segmentation).
- Draft bridge letter language that:
  * Confirms Dedicated (Redwood-managed reserved pools) are in scope for the Type II report;
  * Clarifies burst exceptions (when traffic falls back to shared and whether that path was in the audit period);
  * Outlines recommended customer responsibilities for Private/VPC deployments.

Suggested evidence to attach to Alex ahead of the meeting:
- SOC 2 PDF (latest)
- Short summary doc mapping hosting modes to controls (1–2 pages)
- Bridge letter template (editable)
- Tenant mapping sample (sanitized)

I'll take the draft bridge letter and the controls mapping; Mateo, can you confirm tenant mapping and whether Orchard has any clusters flagged for burst?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: tenant_mapping_example.csv]

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@orchardbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@orchardbank.com>, Sally Cho <sally@auditworks.com>
Date: 2027-07-19T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 evidence and scope question for hosting modes

Alex — following up with the artifacts and a short clarifying note. Attached: Redwood SOC 2 Type II PDF, bridge-letter template, and a sanitized tenant mapping sample. Summary below.

Short answers:
• Hosted (multitenant Redwood API): fully within the SOC 2 Type II scope we issued for the period 2026-07-01 to 2027-06-30.
• Dedicated (Redwood-managed reserved pools): included in the scope when the pool is provisioned and operated by Redwood under the audited control environment. When a Dedicated pool has burst-to-shared fallback, any workload that actually executes on the shared runtime is within scope only if that shared runtime and the fallback path were included in the audit period; otherwise we call it out as a scoped exception and document it in a bridge letter.
• Private/VPC/on-prem: these are customer-managed deployments and therefore fall outside the standard Type II report. We provide a bridge letter/attestation that:
   - Enumerates which control responsibilities remain with Redwood (e.g., control plane integrations we manage), and
   - Which responsibilities are on the customer side (e.g., network controls, host patching).

Requested next steps from our side:
1) If Orchard wants the dedicated pools to be explicitly covered, confirm the tenant_id/project mapping so we can validate the pools were within the audited environment for the audit period.
2) If burst is enabled for any of Orchard's dedicated pools, flag those pools so we can call out the fallback path and provide specific bridge wording.

Attachments (editable): bridge_letter_template.docx — feel free to propose edits.

Links:
• HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/ORCH-8731
• Draft DocuSign (for formal acceptance of the bridge wording): https://docusign.net/CF7-example

Let me know a good time for a 30-minute call (I have availability tomorrow 12–2pm PT).

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Trust & Security
Redwood Inference
[Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026-07-01_to_2027-06-30.pdf, bridge_letter_template.docx, tenant_mapping_example.csv]

From: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@orchardbank.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@orchardbank.com>, Sally Cho <sally@auditworks.com>
Date: 2027-07-19T10:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 evidence and scope question for hosting modes

Thanks Mateo — that helps a lot. Confirming next steps on our side:

• We'll share the tenant/project mapping and flag any pools that have burst enabled by EOD Monday.
• The procurement team will review the bridge-letter template and propose minor edits if needed.
• We'd like the SOC 2 PDF (the one you attached) added to our vendor risk profile and the bridge letter finalized so we can close the control gap for Private/VPC.

Would you and Kimberly be able to join a 30-minute call on Tuesday 7/20 at 11:00am ET to walk the security and procurement teams through the mapping and the proposed language?

Appreciate the clarity — this materially speeds our review.

Best regards,
Alex Ramos
Director, Cloud Security
Orchard Bank
